## The question this session answers

Session 1 froze the definition of done before the run. But runs are not
one-shot. Halfway through, you notice the agent is working from a false premise
— it thinks the legacy queue is writable, and it isn't.

You correct it. Where does that correction live?

If you typed it into a chat window, it lives in a process. Kill the process and
it is gone. Start a fresh agent tomorrow from the same brief and it makes the
same mistake, because nothing you said was ever written down.

> A chat correction disappears. A fact in the rider survives.

## Start from a known state

```{bash}
find runs -mindepth 1 ! -name .gitkeep -delete 2>/dev/null
find control/receipts -name '*.json' -delete 2>/dev/null
cp control/checks/fixtures/solution-stub.mjs working/src/slugify.mjs
echo "reset: no runs, no receipts, candidate red"
```

## The compare

Both lanes start from the same short brief and no previous chat. In the left
lane the operator states a correction and saves it nowhere. In the right lane
the same correction becomes a run event.

```{bash}
bash scripts/demo-compare.sh s2 --mock --seq 2>&1 \
  | sed $'s/\033\[[0-9;]*m//g' \
  | tail -12
```

The left correction dies with the conversation. The right one becomes part of
the record the next agent reads.

---

## Interrupt a run

An **interrupt** stops a run and records the stop position in its log.

```{bash}
node src/loop.ts run --provider smoke --run-id s2-steer --interrupt-after 2 2>&1 | tail -3
```

The process is gone; the run state remains:

```{bash}
node src/loop.ts view s2-steer | grep status
```

### What the interrupt actually recorded

```{bash}
grep run.interrupted runs/s2-steer/events.jsonl
```

::: {.callout-important}
## The point of the whole session

`{"after_turn": 2}` — and nothing else.

The **position** is durable. The **reason** is not. The log knows exactly where
the run stopped and has no idea why. If the cause of the stop was "the legacy
queue is read-only in this environment," that fact exists nowhere except in my
head and a dead terminal.

The supplied `--interrupt-after` cannot record a fact. Building an
`interrupt --fact` is an optional Go-deeper exercise (`prompts/manufacture.md`,
P3).
:::

### The run as a timeline

Each starred line is an operator writing into the record.

```{bash}
node scripts/timeline.mjs runs/s2-steer/events.jsonl 2>&1 \
  | sed $'s/\033\[[0-9;]*m//g'
```

### Resume reads the log, not the process

```{bash}
node src/loop.ts resume s2-steer 2>&1 | tail -4
```

It continued at turn 3. Turns 1 and 2 were not replayed — the event log is the
state, and the process was only ever a way of appending to it.

```{bash}
node control/dr-gate.ts check s2-steer 2>&1 | head -1
node src/loop.ts complete s2-steer 2>&1 | tail -1
cp control/checks/fixtures/solution-stub.mjs working/src/slugify.mjs
```

## A log that *does* carry the fact

The course ships a hand-written exhibit showing what a durable correction looks
like when the harness can record one.

```{bash}
bash sessions/s2-brief-steer/fixtures/make-steering-run.sh 2>&1 | head -2
echo "---"
grep -E 'plan.rejected|run.rebriefed' runs/fx-steering/events.jsonl
```

Two events, two different jobs:

- `plan.rejected` carries the **fact** — *the legacy queue is read-only in this
  environment*
- `run.rebriefed` carries the **new instruction** — retries go through the
  outbox table

A fresh agent reading this log starts with both. A fresh agent reading my
`s2-steer` log above starts with neither.

---

## Steer, or new contract?

The decision at every interrupt:

> Does this new fact correct the **route**, or change the **definition of done**?

| | Goes where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Route correction | the rider | the outcome did not change; only the path to it did |
| Changed result | a **new contract version** | new hash, new run — the gate refuses an edit in place |

Getting this wrong in the second direction is the expensive one. Quietly
widening what "done" means mid-run is how a run succeeds against a target
nobody agreed to. The gate makes it impossible to do accidentally:

```
contract hash mismatch: contract changed after the run was opened
```

---

## Goal and rider

- A **goal** states the result and the operating limits. Short.
- A **rider** holds the detailed context a fresh agent needs. Everything else.

The split exists so the goal stays readable. The worked example:

```{bash}
wc -m prompts/goal-m03.md prompts/rider-m03.md
```

A **fresh agent** starts with no earlier conversation, which is the whole point:
it forces the written brief to carry the work. Anything I "already told it" is
not in the brief, and will not survive.

The optional rider format has six sections: Context, Live evidence, Focus files,
Deliverable (three items max), Fences, Stop-when.
